_comment: Operator declarations that an op-class has NO fault class provoking it, and why. A declared gap is a reviewable engineering position; an UNDECLARED one is the failure opcover exists to catch. Delete an entry the moment a fault class starts provoking that class — opcover reports a stale exemption so resolved gaps cannot pile up and hide the next real one.

exemptions.why: Inverse-only by construction (spec/029 T-029-3): stop-guest exists as start-guest's declared commit-confirmed rollback_op_class — the compensating action the armed revert fires when a started guest fails its confirm window (REQ-2903: the inverse is a first-class mutation through the full chain, so it must be a registered class). No estate fault is legitimately healed by STOPPING a guest, so no fault class provokes it and none should: a fault→stop-guest pairing would teach the agent to down guests as a remediation, which is the blast-radius direction every gate exists to refuse. Its execution path is exercised by the commit-confirm revert drills, not by fault injection.

The only remaining gap, and the starkest case: reload-service has never been proposed ONCE across the entire session ledger. The service-down class added 2026-07-28 does NOT provoke it — stopping a unit is healed by start-service or restart-service, never by a reload. Provoking it needs a CONFIG-DRIFT fault (a unit running with stale on-disk config that a reload would re-read), which is a different injection shape from stop/kill: the unit must stay ACTIVE and merely be wrong, so the fault is invisible to every liveness check the estate has. That is also why it is listed rather than built — a fault nothing detects would drive no proposal and would only add a silent miss to the A1 denominator.

No fault class legitimately provokes it. `disk-fill` USED to be paired here, but that was a FALSE coverage claim: the injected fault is `fallocate` on /var/tmp/tg-tier1-fill.img, a synthetic benchmark artifact. Growing a filesystem to accommodate a rogue 7 GB file is the wrong remediation even where the disk can grow, and on this estate the pool roots are loopback-backed so it cannot — TG was deliberately taught to STOP proposing disk-grow for these (the earlier '33 disk-fill faults propose an inapplicable disk-grow' work). The only correct remediation is removing the injector's own file, which TG must never learn to do: it would teach the agent to delete the benchmark's instrumentation and is a route to deleting arbitrary operator files. Measured 2026-07-28: 74 disk-fill faults, 12 proposals, 1 heal. Provoking disk-grow honestly needs a fault that fills a GROWABLE volume with legitimate data — until that exists, this gap is DECLARED rather than falsely covered.

No fault class provokes a replica scale. The injector synthesizes INFRASTRUCTURE faults (host-down, service-stopped, disk-fill, guest-down); none is legitimately healed by changing a workload's replica count, and each already has its own remediation op-class. A replica scale remediates a workload-CAPACITY condition — a GitOps-managed workload saturated by legitimate demand — which the injector deliberately does not synthesize: driving real saturating load on this shared box would contend with production and the live eval campaigns, and a synthetic under-replication is invisible to every liveness check the estate has (the workload stays UP, merely undersized), the same shape that keeps reload-service's config-drift gap DECLARED rather than built. The class ships embedded (TG-122 slice 3) to make the gitops-mr lane reachable; it stays dark + Shadow + human-merge-gated (the MR the lane opens is never self-merged), so the uncovered rung acts on nothing. Delete this entry the moment a capacity/saturation fault class begins provoking it.

_overlay_note: spec/028 REQ-2818, OVERLAY HALF — DECLARED AS AN OPEN GAP, NOT AS COVERAGE. A ratified overlay op-class carries no faultinjector pairing: the class did not exist when the fault catalog was written, and the estate condition that produced it is by definition one nobody enumerated in advance — that is what makes it EARNED rather than shipped. The embed-export path is what closes the gap: moving the class into the go:embed registry puts it in front of the same review that pairs every other AUTO-capable class with a fault, and until that MR lands the class is capped at auto_notice and never acts silently (ADR-0016 decision 2), so the uncovered rung is the one that still tells a human. WHY THERE IS NO PER-SLUG ENTRY BELOW: opcover reads the registry from opschema.Specs() in the specvalidate process, where NO overlay is loaded — so an exemption naming a ratified slug would be reported as a stale-exemption ('not a registered op-class') on every run. Making these declarable needs opcover to learn about the overlay tamper domain, which is a change to tools/specvalidate/opcover and is not owned by T-028-10. The scenario 'Overlay classes carry a declared opcover exemption' therefore stays PENDING in spec/028's _test_mapping.json rather than being marked covered by this note.
